folate-palak.why: Spinach and moong give folate, iron and protein.
folate-palak.recipe: Cook ½ cup moong dal till soft. Add 2 cups chopped washed palak, a tempering of jeera, garlic and a pinch of haldi; simmer 5 min. Finish with lemon.
folate-palak.do: Wash leafy greens well in running water.
folate-palak.dont: Don’t skip prescribed folic acid tablets.

ginger-nausea.why: Small, frequent meals ease morning sickness.
ginger-nausea.recipe: Keep roasted chana, khakhra or plain rusks by the bed. Eat a few before getting up. Sip water or warm water with a slice of fresh ginger through the day.
ginger-nausea.dont: Can’t keep water down for a day? Call your doctor.

iron-ragi.why: Ragi gives iron and calcium; tomato’s vitamin C helps absorb iron.
iron-ragi.recipe: Mix 1 cup ragi flour, ¼ cup rice flour, curd and water to a thin batter with onion and coriander. Cook thin dosas. Serve with fresh tomato chutney.
iron-ragi.do: Pair iron foods with amla, lemon, guava or tomato.
iron-ragi.dont: Avoid tea or coffee within an hour of meals.

safety-milk.why: Unpasteurised milk and some soft cheeses can carry Listeria.
safety-milk.recipe: Boil loose milk before use. Make paneer at home from boiled milk with lemon juice, or buy sealed, pasteurised paneer.
safety-milk.dont: No raw milk, raw eggs or undercooked meat.

choline-egg.why: Eggs are the richest everyday source of choline; soya and paneer help vegetarians.
choline-egg.recipe: Sauté onion, tomato, haldi and jeera. Add 2 beaten eggs (or crumbled paneer + soaked soya granules). Cook until fully firm. Eat with a roti and salad.
choline-egg.do: Cook eggs until yolk and white are firm.
choline-egg.dont: No half-boiled or raw eggs (including in homemade mayonnaise).

iodine-salt.why: Iodine supports the baby’s thyroid and developing brain.
iodine-salt.recipe: Use iodised salt for everyday cooking and store it in a closed, dry jar away from the stove. Add salt towards the end of cooking.
iodine-salt.do: Moderate amounts; ask your doctor if your BP is high.
iodine-salt.dont: Rock or sea salt usually lacks enough iodine for daily use.

protein-sprouts.why: Sprouts are rich in protein, folate and fibre.
protein-sprouts.recipe: Steam moong sprouts 5–7 min until soft. Toss with chopped cucumber, tomato, roasted jeera, lemon and coriander.
protein-sprouts.dont: Avoid raw sprouts in pregnancy (germ risk).

omega-fish.food: Mackerel (bangda) or sardine curry / walnut-flax ladoo
omega-fish.why: Omega-3 fats build the brain and eyes and lower the risk of early birth.
omega-fish.recipe: Fish: cook bangda or sardine in a tomato–coconut curry until flaky. Vegetarian: blend dates, walnuts and roasted flaxseed; roll small ladoos.
omega-fish.do: Low-mercury fish 2–3 times a week; ask about DHA if vegetarian.
omega-fish.dont: Avoid shark, swordfish, king mackerel (surmai — check locally) and big-eye tuna.

calcium-curd.why: Curd and sesame give calcium for bones and teeth.
calcium-curd.recipe: Mix soft rice with fresh curd and a little milk. Temper with mustard seeds, curry leaves and a spoon of til. Add grated carrot.
calcium-curd.do: Set curd from boiled or pasteurised milk.
calcium-curd.dont: Don’t take calcium and iron tablets together — space them out.

fluids-buttermilk.why: Fluids help with constipation, swelling and urine infections.
fluids-buttermilk.recipe: Chaas: whisk curd with water, roasted jeera, a pinch of salt and mint. Nimbu pani: lemon, water, a little jaggery, pinch of salt.
fluids-buttermilk.do: 8–10 glasses of fluid a day unless told otherwise.
fluids-buttermilk.dont: Limit sugary drinks and packaged juices.

b12-dairy.why: Dairy gives vitamin B12, protein and calcium to vegetarians.
b12-dairy.recipe: Stuff whole-wheat dough with mashed paneer, peas, coriander and jeera. Cook on a tawa with a little ghee. Serve with curd.
b12-dairy.do: Ask your doctor about a B12 check if you are vegetarian.

caffeine.why: Too much caffeine is best avoided in pregnancy.
caffeine.recipe: Swap your second tea or coffee for warm haldi milk (from boiled milk), jeera water, or fresh coconut water.
caffeine.do: Under 200 mg caffeine a day ≈ 1 mug of coffee or 2–3 cups of tea.
caffeine.dont: Watch energy drinks and colas — they add up.

tastes-home.why: Varied home flavours reach the amniotic fluid; baby gets to ‘taste’ your family’s food.
tastes-home.recipe: Cook toor dal with pumpkin, drumstick, carrot and beans. Add tamarind, sambar powder and a curry-leaf tempering. Eat with rice or idli.
tastes-home.do: Eat a rainbow of seasonal vegetables.
tastes-home.dont: Avoid very spicy, oily food if you have heartburn.

fibre-poha.why: Poha (with lemon) gives iron; peanuts add protein and choline; vegetables add fibre.
fibre-poha.recipe: Rinse thick poha. Sauté mustard, curry leaves, onion, peas and carrot; add haldi, poha and roasted peanuts. Finish with lemon and coriander.
fibre-poha.do: Add a fruit for vitamin C.

mindful-meal.why: Eating slowly helps you notice hunger and fullness.
mindful-meal.recipe: Once this week, eat one meal without screens. Notice colours, smells and textures. Put the spoon down between bites. Tell baby what you are eating.
mindful-meal.dont: Don’t eat lying down if you have heartburn.

kheer-trad.why: Milk gives calcium and protein. Classical texts recommended milk-based gruels in late pregnancy (heritage note, page 27).
kheer-trad.recipe: Cook 3 tbsp broken wheat or rice in 2 cups boiled milk until soft. Sweeten lightly with jaggery; add cardamom and chopped nuts.
kheer-trad.do: Small portions, as part of a balanced day.
kheer-trad.dont: If you have diabetes in pregnancy, ask before adding sweets.

dates-energy.why: Til, jaggery and dates give iron and energy for the last weeks.
dates-energy.recipe: Roast til and chopped nuts; mix with melted jaggery and chopped dates; press into a plate and cut squares. One piece is a portion.
dates-energy.do: Keep healthy snacks ready for the hospital bag.
dates-energy.dont: Mind the portion — jaggery is still sugar.
